 Market Scorecard Since Trump Inauguration: Gains, Losses, Arrogance, And Ignorance
 Nov 02, 2026, 9:40 AM ET State Street SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (SPY) , IVV , VOO , SP500 , SPX , NDX , QQQ , DIA , DJI , IWM 10 Comments 1 Like Sungarden Investment Publishing 12.01K Followers Follow Summary
 The article reviews market performance since President Trump's inauguration, highlighting notable gains and losses across sectors.
 I analyze how political events, policy decisions, and market sentiment have influenced asset prices and sector rotation.
 Arrogance and ignorance among investors and policymakers have led to both outsized gains and avoidable losses.
 I emphasize the importance of humility, vigilance, and adaptability in navigating politically charged markets.
 franckreporter/iStock via Getty Images
 The Grateful Dead said it best: What a long, strange trip it's been.
 This article details the macro/overview results of the first two years of the second Trump Presidency. That is, since his January 20, 2025, inauguration.

 This article was written by
 Sungarden Investment Publishing 12.01K Followers Follow I'm Rob Isbitts. My late father, a DIY investor, taught me to chart stocks when I was 16. I used that early coaching for 3 decades as a CIO, investment advisor, writer and mentor, including being named a Top 100 US Wealth Managers by Worth Magazine 4 times. I sold my investment management firm in 2020 to focus on research, and delivering my investment process to a wider audience. Now semi-retired, I publish here as well as at Barchart.com and ETFYourself.com, the Substack site I created. My technical analysis and portfolio-building approach is available to DIY investors and financial advisors at ROAR.PiTrade.com. My investing approach is straightforward, but not at all common. I am defense-first, and I use a wide range of investments, including nearly every type of ETF. As a semi-retired Baby Boomer, I created the Hedged Bond model portfolio to help show investors how to capitalize on the highest interest rates in a generation, while managing interest rate volatilty. My goals at this stage of my career are to share my experience and skeptical eye with humility, discipline, and a non-traditional approach to modern markets.I welcome interaction with readers here, as long as they are serious, delivered professionally, and with an intention to further the conversation for the community here.
